newsitem.title: GERMANY: Puma shares jump on takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Puma shares jump on takeover talk.

text.p: Shares in German sportswear maker Puma AG raced over six percent higher in Frankfurt bourse trade on Monday underpinned by market talk that Italian fashion giant Benetton might be in the market to buy the group.
The shares jumped to 56.50 marks in bourse trade but closed at 54.90 marks.
"There has been talk that Benetton is interested in Puma and that is what has been driving the share price," said one Frankfurt-based analysts who asked not to be named.
Puma officials said they were unable to comment on the matter, saying only they could not find an explanation for the strong share price move.
Benetton was not immediately available for comment.
This rise occured despite news that U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs and German bank Commerzbank both downgraded the group's shares after Friday's half-year results.
Commerzbank put Puma on hold after having had them on buy while Goldman Sachs labeled the shares market performer.
"It cannot be those numbers pushing the Puma shares," a dealer said, adding the company posted less than stellar results on Friday.
On the other hand analysts said that while they had no reason to believe Benetton had made a bid for Puma, the suggestion was not entirely ludicrous.
"This is not wholly implausible," said another analyst who also asked not to be named.
Speculating on where the share price might move in coming days, traders and analysts said this depended largely on what happens with the takeover rumours.
"If one of the two companies comes out and says there is really nothing to the talk and the market believes this, then the euphoria in Puma shares will evaporate very quickly," a dealer said.
